newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says not hopeful on Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says not hopeful on Islamists.

text.p: A minister from the conservative wing of Turkey's coalition government said on Thursday he was not hopeful that the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP) would support measures to crack down on Islamist activism.
The comments by Health Minister Yildirim Aktuna pushed shares in Istanbul down 5.75 percent on the day in afternoon trading over concerns about the future of the coalition.

"Personally, I am certainly not hopeful about RP. I do not think they will show understanding and be helpful to us," Aktuna was quoted as by state-run Anatolian news agency at a hospital clinic opening ceremony.
Turkey's military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) last month issued a series of orders aimed at stemming the rising prominence of Islamist activities in public life.
The country's first Islamist prime minister and RP leader Necmettin Erbakan signed up to the proposals despite unease within his party about the proposed measures.
"For RP to accept the NSC decisions means giving up the policies which they have followed until today," Aktuna said.
